breathStream.note: The dragon’s attack is a CONTINUOUS stream that must always reach its target. Assemble it, do not stretch a single cone: root at the maw, ceil((dist-28-19)/16) mid tiles, tip on the target face. All parts of one run share ONE frame index — that is what keeps the joins invisible; the pattern shifting frame to frame is the flow. A continuous stream needs no separate impact burst: the tip part IS the contact effect, so fire impact_burn once at onset at most.
breathStream.seamRule: same frame index across root, all mid tiles and tip

targeting.giant: walls first with the melee slab (state: attack), then defences from range with the boulder (state: throw)
targeting.dragon: continuous fire stream at any range (state: breath) — never falls short
targeting.cannon: ground troops within range; aim then fire then reload
targeting.mortar: ground troops at range — high-arc splash. Cannot hit what is close: the arc means a minimum range, unlike the cannon.
targeting.mage: defences and clustered troops at range. `cast` is the single-target bolt; `channel` is the AOE ring and is the reason to bring one.
targeting.bilgewraith: BURROWS UNDER WALLS and surfaces inside the compound, where it targets MINES first. It does not fight its way through a wall — it goes under it, which is the whole unit.
targeting.troll: troops and walls in melee. `attack` is a horizontal SWEEP for troops; `pound` is both fists into the ground for buildings. Highest HP line in the roster and it visibly regenerates.
targeting.turrider: closes distance fast and hits once, hard. `charge` is a LOOP and is the movement state; `attack` is the lance strike out of it. It is the only mounted unit in the game.
targeting.tunneler: goes UNDER walls like the bilgewraith, but as an engineer rather than a ghost: it excavates a timbered shaft and does structural damage with a pick. Same state machine, opposite treatment.
targeting.plunderer: storages. It is not a fighter — it reaches the vault, fills its sack, and leaves. Its `haul` term is a state an integrator must carry: empty out, full home.
targeting.bowman: troops and troops-first, at range. `draw` holds on its last frame while it waits for a target; `loose` fires on f0.
targeting.direwyvern: AREA DENIAL. The firestorm is a FAN across an arc of ground, not a jet down one line, and it leaves fx_burnfield burning behind it — the damage is the zone, not the hit. Strictly larger and stronger than the player dragon at every tier.
targeting.gloamfang: HUNTS DEFENDERS. Prefers defending troops and heroes over buildings, and CLEARS WALLS with its `leap` state rather than pathing round them — a wall does not stop it, only something that can fight it does.

attachments: Emitter points are PUBLISHED per atlas cell (see `emitters` on the dragon breath/spit and cannon idle/aim/fire/reload atlases) because "pin it to the mouth" is not a spec. They are projected from the same rig node and camera the sprite is drawn with, so they cannot drift from the art. The mortar publishes `emitters.muzzle` the same way the cannon does.
mortarNote: The mortar is built as a RING, not a tube. Every other defence reads as a line (cannon = barrel out, towers = vertical shaft); a near-upright bombard presents its open bore to the elev-42 camera as a big dark ellipse inside a bronze lip, which is a silhouette nothing else in the set has and which survives down to 24px. Aim reads as the bombard LEANING toward its target, not as it pointing — a near-vertical weapon swept through a full circle would look identical in all eight aims.
mageNote: The mage is the only troop in the roster with NO LEGS: an unbroken bell-shaped robe running to the ground, hovering. Every other troop resolves at 32px to "torso on two legs", so a robed human drawn that way shares its outline with ten other units. The bell, the staff taller than the figure, and the lit shard above the hood are the three things carrying the read — nothing else is allowed to out-value them.
bilgewraithNote: The burrow cycle is the unit. `burrow` -> `tunnel` (LOOP) -> `surface`. In `tunnel` NO BODY IS DRAWN: the point of an infiltrator is that the defender cannot see it, so the sprite honours that and shows only a travelling mound. Its silhouette tell is the tricorn, built wider than its own shoulders — nothing else in the game has a horizontal spike either side of the head.
palette: Unit ramps sit on the user-approved hexes from NEW assets/HANDOFF-NEW.md, on the 1/2/3 rungs of each 8-tone PAL ramp: Dragon Scale #274A40/#3E7A67/#6FB89B (dg1-3), Giant Bronze #5C3A28/#8C6244/#BC9268 (gn1-3), Arcane Purple #2E2447/#5B4389/#9377C9 (mg1-3), Brine #25423F/#3E6D68/#6FA39D (br1-3). Darks below and lights above are derived from those at a consistent ratio. The mage`s energy ramp (ar) is anchored to the same family — ar/arM/arL are #5B4389/#9377C9/#C9A6F5, which is exactly what the shipped fx_aoe_burst, ovl_aoe_r3 and fx_fire_magetower masters are drawn in, so a reworked mage colour-matches the Mage Tower casting the same spell. Batch 17 adds tl (Troll Hide, approved) and sk/tp (rider steel from the original 16, plus tur pelt on the Stone tones). Batch 18 adds cr (plunderer crimson, anchored on the shipped master`s #8F2C2C) and gr (bowman greens on the house Deep Pine #2E4636 / Highland Green #567A4B); the tunneler reuses the rider`s sk steel and the ert earth ramp.
trollNote: Written against the giant, point by point, because two epic melee brutes must not share a silhouette. Giant: symmetric, long-armed, carries a stone slab, slams overhead. Troll: ASYMMETRIC — one overgrown arm and one withered — with a spinal ridge of keratin plates, no weapon at all, and a horizontal sweep. The asymmetry is the read and it survives every facing. Its palette is the approved Troll Hide (#43473A / #6E7660 / #9FA88C) on tl1/tl2/tl3.
turriderNote: The only QUADRUPED in the game, and that is the whole design. Every other unit is a biped, so four legs is a silhouette nothing else can be confused with at any size or facing. The tur carries the outline and the rider sits INSIDE it — a rider tall enough to break the top line would turn this back into a biped on a box. The backswept ridged horns are the second read and the difference between this and a horse. Steel is the original-16 armour pair (#54677A / #BBD0D6) on sk2/sk4.
tunnelerNote: Shares the bilgewraith`s burrow/tunnel/surface machine, so the TREATMENT is what separates them and it is deliberate. The wraith SINKS and leaves a raw mound; the tunneler EXCAVATES and leaves works — spoil heaped outside a squared collar, timber props standing in it, a lintel, and the lamp still glowing in the mouth during `tunnel`. Its silhouette is wide-and-low with a flat helm, where every other biped in the roster is taller than it is wide, and it carries the only warm point light of any troop.
plundererNote: The unit is its cargo. `haul` runs 0 -> 1 across `loot` and drives the sack`s size, its swing lag, and the body`s counter-lean — so a glance tells you whether this one has been to the vault. Nothing else in the roster carries cargo, and unlike a weapon the sack is legible from BEHIND, which matters because this is the troop players watch running away.
bowmanNote: The bow is the unit and a bow is a CURVE — the one shape left unclaimed (mage = bell, rider = quadruped, tunneler = wide block, plunderer = lumpy sack, troll = asymmetric mass). It is drawn taller than the archer and held clear of the torso so the arc is never occluded, with the quiver breaking the OPPOSITE shoulder so left and right of the silhouette do different jobs. A bow is a spring and must be seen to load: the limbs bend across `draw`, the string is a hard V (never a curve — a curved string reads as slack), and on `loose` f0 it snaps flat with a blurred doubled string and the arrow gone.

roster.highlander: Line infantry — the roster BASELINE. Every other troop was given an escape from "torso on two legs"; this one owns that shape deliberately. Its two unclaimed reads: a two-handed claymore held CENTRED (every other weapon is carried to one side) and a kilt hem at the knee with bare legs below (the mage bell is unbroken to the ground). Also the only bare head in the roster.
roster.kegrunner: Demolition — carries a bomb and dies delivering it. run -> prime -> detonate, and DETONATE IS THE DEATH. Smallest troop in the game, hunched so far over the keg that its head sits below the top of the cargo. The lit fuse is the only light in the game that COUNTS DOWN: it shortens, brightens and accelerates from one `fuse` term that also drives lean and stride.
roster.gloamfang: Dark shock melee. A BIPED BUILT WRONG on purpose: shoulders are the highest point (every other biped is head-topped), arms longer than legs, digitigrade back-bent knees, and the only tail on a biped in the game. Deliberately NOT a quadruped — the tur rider owns that shape. Its `howl` inverts the whole silhouette for six frames, head up and back above the shoulders, which is what makes a buff visible instead of numeric.
roster.direwyvern: Dark heavy AOE flier. Built as the dragon’s opposite along every axis that shows: a horizontal slab against a serpentine curve, a permanent wide glide against a beat, slow and committed against fast and agile, and a FAN of fire across an arc against a jet down one line. The wingspan is the unit — the broadest silhouette in the game, and because it barely beats, that bar holds still.
roster.hexbarrow: Dark siege. Huge damage to walls and buildings, and it disgorges TEN barrowlings roughly every 15s. Silhouette claim is WHEELS — nothing else in the game has them. The gun points slightly DOWN (it shoots walls), which separates the three siege weapons at a glance: hexbarrow down, tower cannon flat, mortar near-vertical. A hex-mage rides the tiller, which is the one arcane light on an ember faction.
roster.barrowling: Dark swarm, spawned ten at a time by the Hexbarrow. Fast, goes for defences. Authored to be legible in a MASS rather than interesting alone: the read is an oversized head with ember eyes, which is all that survives at 16px in a pile of ten. Ships four baked VARIANTS in the column axis — deal them out, because ten identical sprites read as wallpaper.

factions.dark: DARK TROOPS — a fifth attacker family, defined by VALUE rather than hue. They share the `dk` ramp (the house neutrals o/o2/oS on the same 1/2/3 rungs every other unit ramp uses, extended upward) and carry exactly one saturated accent: ember, from the fl tones that already ship. A faction that shares a hue with nobody and a value band with nobody is legible before any detail resolves.

payload.note: Measured, not estimated: per-unit B/px sampled from the shipped files, applied to each atlas’ real drawn area. SVG masters are NOT the delivery format — see deliveryFormat.
payload.gzipRatio: 5.4x measured on the direwyvern atlases, 4.6x on the giant — NOT the 10-20x usually assumed for text formats, because these are already run-length-encoded path strings with little residual redundancy
payload.deliveryFormat: RASTERISE AT BUILD TIME. These SVGs are authoring masters: one <path> per palette tone, run-length h/v runs, integer coords. A mobile/Seeker client should ship PNG or KTX2 spritesheets generated from them, not the SVGs. At 1x a direwyvern firestorm sheet is 2432x1664 -> ~1.2MB as indexed PNG against 4.74MB of SVG.
